title: Development: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Push past recall — evaluate Piaget like a grade 9 candidate.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology exam stretch on development: evaluation, AO2 application and AO3 analysis of Piaget.
final_note: You can now argue both sides of Piaget with named evidence.

concepts.def: Social constructivist stressing culture and language.
Gap between what a child can do alone and with help.
Adult support gradually removed as a child learns.

walkthroughs.body_html: Strengths: influenced education, lots of supporting evidence, universal stages observed cross-culturally. Weaknesses: Hughes showed he underestimated children, his samples were small and biased, and he ignored social-cultural factors highlighted by Vygotsky.

Piaget: child as lone scientist, biologically driven stages. Vygotsky: child as apprentice, learning through culture and a More Knowledgeable Other. Vygotsky's scaffolding and ZPD explain how teaching accelerates development.

'Mia thinks her tall glass has more juice than her brother's wide glass.' Identify the stage (preoperational) and the limitation (lack of conservation). Then evaluate using Hughes to suggest Piaget underestimated children.
